use_case_name: Associate Related Surveillance Tracks and Points

claims.content: To enable the C2 JU to manually correlate subsurface surveillance data and associate related tracks or points by using the J7.7 Track Association message when two Track Numbers (TNs) are determined to report information for the same target.

goal.raw_text: To enable the C2 JU to manually correlate subsurface surveillance data and associate related tracks or points by using the J7.7 Track Association message when two Track Numbers (TNs) are determined to report information for the same target.

claims.content: C2 JU
The C2 JU has identified two tracks that are eligible for correlation, meaning they may represent the same object and require resolution of dual designations.
The C2 JU is capable of transmitting and receiving all response values of the J7.2 message for real-time air and/or surface tracks held locally by their system.

No automatic correlation restrictions apply — specifically: (a) no Identity (ID) conflict exists between the two tracks; (b) if Mode II codes differ, the local Mode II code is not current or inhibition capability is not active; (c) both tracks are not locally derived real-time tracks being updated with local positional data; (d) neither track has Strength field set to a value greater than 1 unless set to No Statement.

If one of the tracks is a remote report being tested for correlation and is a J2.0 Indirect PPLI message with Originator E/C field set to 0 (Surface) or 3 (Air), it shall be processed for correlation like a J3.2 air or J3.3 surface (maritime) track with TQ = 7.
Subsurface tracks are excluded from correlation with IUs, so any track involved must not be subsurface.
The C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation and initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.

trigger.raw_text: The C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation and initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.

claims.content: The C2 JU determines that two Track Numbers (TNs) are being used to report information for the same target and initiates a J7.7 Track Association message.
The C2 JU transmits the J7.7 Track Association message to request manual correlation of the subsurface surveillance data.
If the receiving C2 JU receives a J7.2 message with RV field set to value 3, it shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the specified restrictions applies.
Upon acceptance of the manual correlation, the resulting track shall not be subject to automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
If a correlation is not found, the C2 JU shall integrate the received J2 PPLI report into its surveillance database as part of the surveillance picture.

If 32 messages are not received subsequent to this action and the receiving C2 JU still has no local data, the C2 JU assumes no responsibility for reporting the subject IU on the Surveillance Network PG.
If the position or other data in a PPLI meet a system’s decorrelation criteria, the PPLI and local track data shall be decorrelated.
After decorrelation, the C2 JU shall initiate a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.
The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field shall both be reported as No Statement.

If a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds, the C2 JU shall assume R2 of an IU (including C2 and non-C2 JUs and forwarded FUs and RUs) in accordance with real-time track reporting rules.
If a J2 PPLI message, other than J2.0, is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, the C2 JU shall assume R2 of an IU.
If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FU for a FU, SU, or other IU, the C2 JU shall assume R2 of an IU.
If the Geodetic Position Quality in the J2 PPLI message is set to value 0, the C2 JU shall assume R2 of an IU.
A C2 JU assuming R2 of an IU reports it as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG; the type of surveillance message depends upon the Environment/Category of the IU being reported.
The Identity shall be reported as Friend; the Track Number, Platform and Platform Activity values received in previous PPLI messages shall be reported.
The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator shall be reported as value 1, and shall be maintained if another C2 JU assumes R2 of the IU.
When the RV field is set to value 0 in a J7.2 Correlation message, it indicates a reverse correlation would be acceptable.
When the RV field is set to value 1 in a J7.2 Correlation message, it indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected.

Receiving IUs desiring to reverse the requested correlation use the RV field to determine if a reverse correlation request should be originated or if the original correlation request should be rejected.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.
When the RV field is set to value 3, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.

If a correlation is found with a track for which the C2 JU has R2 and the TNs are different, the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted, with the Source TN in the header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.

If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R2 and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message shall be discarded.
Subsurface tracks shall not be correlated with IUs.

There is an OCC on the Dropped TN as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.(g)(i) and the received RV field is set to value 0; the reverse correlation shall be transmitted if the new Dropped TN has no correlation constraint. If both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation shall be rejected.
There is an OCC on the Dropped TN as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.(g)(i) and the received RV field is set to value 1; in this case, the correlation shall be rejected.

C2 JUs receiving or generating a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2, Correlation Rejection, shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2(1-10,1) minutes.
When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
An operator alert in the event of the rejection of an automatic correlation shall be a system option.

C2 JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies, in which case the correlation shall be rejected: (a) The two tracks are of a different E/C, or either track has an existing s/c conflict; (b) One track is simulated and the other is live; (c) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
The C2 JU has accepted the requested correlation of the tracks.
The resulting track is not subject to automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
